body:
Current 10.4.3 reads:

> **10.4.3** Verify that the authorization code is short‑lived. The maximum lifetime can be up to 10 minutes for L1 and L2 applications and up to 1 minute for L3 applications.

Reading:

* [this thread](https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/browse/oauth/?q=browser%20swapping&gbt=1&index=);
* the [ConsentFix](https://pushsecurity.com/blog/consentfix) attack description;
* issue [230](https://github.com/oauth-wg/oauth-v2-1/pull/230) on Oauth 2.1,

I think it would make sense to reduce this to 1 minutes / 30 seconds.

comments.body:
For L1 - I don't care too much.

For L2 and L3, it is at the moment 1 minute. Is it one minute or 30 seconds? I think it is not that drastic a change to take risks down.

As reducing the time would also be a breaking change, it makes sense to follow changes in the related specs at the time when we are going to release the next major release.

title: Reduce maximum lifetime of OAuth authorization code (10.4.3)
